lots.guide_summary: All surviving evidence is SOLD; no verified UNSOLD or ASKING survives. Close entries run $85 (1200D body, Gowans) and $100 (100D body, Gowans) up to a single $850 for an 1100D twin-lens kit at a Sydney Airport lost-property sale, which looks like an outlier. Category guides at Gowans: $30-160. Realistic Gowans hammer for this lot looks like about $80-140. All AUD, no conversion.
lots.working: Only one same-model SOLD result exists (Theodore Bruce $850, Jun 2025), and it is a different kit (two Canon lenses) sold in a lost-property sale where bidding runs hot; using it would give keep max 850/1.198 = 709, which no other evidence supports, so I have not used it. The Gowans results are sibling models, not the same item, so by the rules no formal maximum is set. Informal guide only: the lowest close sibling result is $85 (1200D body) and $85/1.198 = $70.95, so about $70 hammer ($84 all-in) would be in line with local buyers; the Tamron 70-300 and bag add a little. Flip: no same-item resale evidence (eBay closed to us), so 0.
lots.confidence_reason: Body identified from the rear button layout (badge not legible), lens read on cap and barrel. Only one same-model SOLD entry and it is an outlier; the rest are sibling or category comps. Untested, shutter count unknown.
lots.dropped_entries: eBay AU AU$289 and AU$243.18 asking (snippet only; eBay returns 403 to us, cannot verify, kept only as a lead). Gumtree ACT $170 negotiable asking (Gumtree returned 403, snippet only, lead only). Theodore Bruce entry kept but upgraded from snippet to page-verified and flagged as an outlier. Gowans 400D lot downgraded from close to category guide.
lots.key_photo_findings: Rear of body shows the 1100D layout: DISP top right, ISO above the cross keys, live view button with red dot, AF right, MENU and WB below, Canon logo top left of the screen. Front: Canon badge, mode dial, pop-up flash. Lens barrel reads 70-300mm 1:4-5.6 TELE-MACRO with a TAMRON band and TAMRON cap, so it is a Tamron AF 70-300mm Di LD Macro with petal-free round hood. Charger or AC adapter in the bag, Canon EOS strap. No 18-55mm lens seen. Rear LCD has light dust and smudges.
lots.condition: Used, untested. Cosmetically tidy in photos, LCD dusty. Battery presence, charger type, shutter count and whether it powers up unknown.
lots.question_for_gowans: Is the camera an EOS 1100D (badge on the front), does it power on with the included battery, is there a battery in the camera, and is the black box a charger or an AC adapter? Is there any other lens in the bag besides the Tamron 70-300mm?

lots.guide_summary: Same or close entries run A$307 to A$375: three SOLD (Gowans $307 hammer Jul 2026; US eBay tested units A$363 and A$375 at 1 USD = 1.4328 AUD) and one ASKING (RetroSales $329.99, tested). No UNSOLD found. Standard black original Xbox bundles make $110-160 at Gowans, so the crystal shell roughly doubles it.
lots.working: Keep: lowest same-item SOLD in the last 24 months is Gowans $307 (Jul 2026). 307 / 1.198 = 256.26, round down to $255 hammer ($305.49 all-in). Caution: ours is sold AS IS and untested, the $307 unit was not marked as is, so bidding to the full $255 assumes it works. Flip: likely resale about A$330 on eBay AU for a working crystal with two controllers and two games (between Gowans $307 hammer and US A$363-375 tested). Less eBay fees about 13% ($43) and outbound postage about $30 for a heavy console: 330 - 43 - 30 = 257. 257 / 2.396 = 107.3, round down to $105. Flip only works if it tests good.
lots.confidence_reason: Crystal shell and XBOX jewel clearly visible and three SOLD pages opened, but the unit is untested and as is, and I cannot see the underside label to confirm a factory crystal unit.

lots.question_for_gowans: Does the Xbox power on and read a disc? Is the clear controller a Microsoft one, and are both the power cable and AV cable included? What does the label underneath say (model or crystal edition)?
